description: Fig. 4 is a ten-panel composite of DFT electron-density contour maps for the Fe1-xMnxAl system, laid out as two columns of five rows: the left column (a, c, e, g, i) shows total electron density distribution contours and the right column (b, d, f, h, j) shows electron density difference distribution contours, each left/right pair belonging to one crystallographic slice. Pair (a)/(b) is FeAl-(011); (c)/(d) Fe Mn Al-(011); (e)/(f) and (g)/(h) are both labelled Fe Mn Al-(110); (i)/(j) Mn–Al-(110). Every panel is a 2D colour contour map drawn over a plane marked with a small X/Y/Z axis triad and carries a vertical "Slice 1" colour bar with printed contour values — (a) 0.075–0.750, (b) −0.030–0.060, (c) 0.120–0.560, (d) −0.07–0.08, (e) and (g) 0.120–0.500, (f) −0.060–0.050, (h) −0.07–0.08, (i) 0.10–0.50, (j) −0.05–0.05. Spheres are coloured by species per the bottom legend: Al purple, Fe blue-grey, Mn green. In the total-density maps atoms occupy red high-density cores separated by green/blue interstitial regions; in the difference maps red and blue lobes and elongated contours run along the Al–Fe, Al–Mn and Fe–Mn bond axes. Together the panels demonstrate combined covalent and metallic bonding in Fe–Mn–Al alloys.

FeAl-(011) electron density difference contour map; red/orange positive lobes around atoms and blue negative regions in the interstitials; 'Slice 1' colour bar spans −0.030 to 0.060.
Fe Mn Al-(011) total electron density map; four red circular high-density cores around green Mn and blue-grey Fe spheres on a green/blue background; colour bar 0.120–0.560; axis triad X/Z.
Fe Mn Al-(011) electron density difference map; red and blue elongated lobes around the atoms; colour bar −0.07 to 0.08.
Fe Mn Al-(110) total electron density map; red cores with green haloes, similar topology to (c)/(g); colour bar 0.120–0.500; axis triad Z/Y.
Fe Mn Al-(110) electron density difference map; red lobes and blue interstitial regions; colour bar −0.060 to 0.050; axis triad Z/Y.
Second map labelled Fe Mn Al-(110) total electron density (caption repeats the (110) plane of (e)); red cores with green haloes; colour bar 0.120–0.500; axis triad X/Y.
Second map labelled Fe Mn Al-(110) electron density difference; red/blue lobes about the atoms; colour bar −0.07 to 0.08.
Mn–Al-(110) total electron density map; red circular cores around green Mn spheres on green/blue background; colour bar 0.10–0.50; axis triad Z/X.
Mn–Al-(110) electron density difference map; red/blue lobes with elongated features; colour bar −0.05 to 0.05; axis triad X/Y.

observations.observation: The figure contains ten contour-map panels arranged in two columns of five rows.
A legend at the bottom of the figure assigns sphere colours: Al purple, Fe blue-grey, Mn green.
Each panel carries a vertical colour bar titled 'Slice 1' with printed numeric contour values, but no unit is printed on any bar.
Panel (a) total electron density colour scale runs 0.075 to 0.750, the highest range in the figure.
Difference maps (b, d, f, h, j) have colour scales spanning negative to positive values (e.g. (b) −0.030 to 0.060; (d) and (h) −0.07 to 0.08).
The caption labels the ten panels: a, b FeAl-(011); c, d Fe Mn Al-(011); e, f Fe Mn Al-(110); g, h Fe Mn Al-(110); i, j Mn–Al-(110).
The caption assigns the left column to total electron density distribution contours and the right column to electron density difference distribution contours.
The citing text states that the elongated contours along the Al–Fe, Al–Mn and Fe–Mn bond axes in the total electron density maps indicate covalent interactions exist.
The citing text states that some electrons are delocalized and distributed throughout the circular map between Al, Mn and Fe atoms, indicating covalent and metallic bonding features.
The citing text states electrons located around Mn, Fe and Al atoms are indicated in blue colour, showing covalent bonds between the atoms.

The citing text concludes the Fe–Mn–Al alloys combine covalent and metallic bonding and have weaker covalent bond effects, which could lead to high melting points and high hardness, and that the alloys have magnetic characteristics.

In the total-electron-density panels the atoms sit inside red high-value cores separated by green-to-blue lower-value interstitial channels; the difference panels show red positive and blue negative lobes around the same atom positions.
The panel labels 'e, f Fe Mn Al-(110)' and 'g, h Fe Mn Al-(110)' in the caption describe the same plane, so one of the two pairs is ambiguous.

electron density difference (Slice 1 contour values, arbitrary units)
